text: dsh-session-grove 是面向 DSH Desktop Web 客户端的侧栏插件，在现有工作区侧栏中加入自由分组视图。它允许把来自不同工作区的会话归入同一分组，并通过创建、重命名和移动分组来整理列表；拖放也可调整会话位置。分组归属由插件单独保存，适合希望跨工作区归类会话的用户。代码未显示需要 API Key 或外部服务。

dsh-session-grove adds a custom groups view to the DSH Desktop sidebar. Users can group sessions across workspaces, create or rename groups, and move sessions with drag and drop. Assignments are stored separately by the plugin; the code shows no API key or external service requirement.
想把不同工作区的 DSH 会话放进同一组里管理。
DSH 侧栏能不能切换成我自己整理的会话分组？
I want to sort my DSH sessions into custom groups across workspaces.
dsh-session-grove 的功能「跨工作区自由分组」：在侧栏的分组视图中创建和命名分组，把不同工作区的会话归到同一组，并通过拖放重新安排会话。切换侧栏视图即可使用；分组归属保存在插件自己的记录中。

dsh-session-grove README · dsh-session-grove：[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A free-form grouping layer over the shipped DSH Desktop workspace/session sidebar. Official workspace and session management remain authoritative: each session keeps its workspace membership and log, while this plugin stores a separate group assignment. A group can therefore contain sessions from different workspaces.

dsh-session-grove README · dsh-session-grove：Current version: **0.4.0-beta.58**  
Primary support: **DSH core/API `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.5** (`engines.dsh: >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`)  
Verified shells: **community DSH Desktop Stable 2.0.18** (rc.2) and **official DeepSeek Harness desktop 0.2.1.0** (rc.5, isolated runtime A+)  
Not supported or promised: **community DSH Desktop Beta** and **community DSH NEXT (`-next` channel)**

dsh-session-grove README · dsh-session-grove：Localization: **English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Russian, Hindi, Traditional Chinese and Arabic** dictionaries are packaged. Locale ids resolve by base language (`ja-JP` → `ja`, `zh-Hant`/`zh-TW` → `zh-Hant`, `pt-BR` → `pt`); unsupported languages fall back to English. Arabic switches the plugin root to RTL and includes the core list/header/dialog RTL overrides. Session count and expand labels use CLDR plural templates. The plugin registers every dictionary with the host, but does not add languages to the host catalog itself.

dsh-session-grove README · dsh-session-grove：Dependency policy: official `@deepseek-ai/*` runtime packages are declared as `peerDependencies`; the DSH host supplies them instead of the plugin bundling a duplicate copy.

See [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) for the support contract, the `engines.dsh` range, the `dsh-0.2` adapter selector and runtime capability checks.

dsh-session-grove README · Platform support：The runtime is platform-neutral JavaScript. It does not invoke PowerShell and has no `process.platform` or `child_process` branches in `src/`. The PowerShell files under `scripts/qa/` are maintainer-only test harnesses and are not shipped in the npm package.

Current verification status:

dsh-session-grove README · Platform support：| Platform | Node/unit tests | Build/package | Real DSH UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | verified locally | verified locally | verified locally |
| Linux | verified by CI | verified by CI | not verified |
| macOS | verified by CI | verified by CI | not verified |

dsh-session-grove README · Platform support：The current CI runs the Node-level gate on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS; the coverage gate runs only on Ubuntu. It is not a cross-platform DSH UI certification: the real DSH UI has been verified on Windows only, so Linux/macOS UI support remains experimental until a real host/UI pass exists. Ordinary users install through dshmarket; the local tarball and CLI are maintainer/debug paths only.

dsh-session-grove README · Platform support：Compatibility is defined by the bundled DSH core/API, not by the desktop shell name. The official and community desktop clients bundle their own DSH versions and plugin compositions; both supported desktop families must be tested separately against this plugin.

Supported desktop scope:

dsh-session-grove README · Platform support：| Desktop | Status |
|---|---|
| community DSH Desktop **Stable** 2.0.18 | verified (rc.2) |
| official DeepSeek Harness desktop 0.2.1.0 | verified (rc.5, isolated A+ and maintainer desktop-window acceptance) |
| community DSH Desktop **Beta** | not supported; no compatibility promise |
| community DSH **NEXT** (`-next` channel) | not supported; no compatibility promise |

dsh-session-grove README · Platform support：The official verification covers the official bundle's DSH host/core in an isolated web-profile instance plus maintainer acceptance on the installed desktop profile. It is not a certification of every third-party plugin combination in that profile.

Beta and NEXT may happen to load the plugin, but their results are not a release gate and do not extend the support contract.

dsh-session-grove README · First run：A one-time card explains that groups only change display placement and how to create groups and drag sessions. The card can be dismissed and its state is stored in `localStorage`. When there are no groups and no sessions, an empty-state action creates the first group.

dsh-session-grove README · dshmarket (recommended)：Install from **dshmarket** and search for:

```text
dsh-session-grove
```

The market entry is being prepared. Once it is listed, install and update the plugin entirely through dshmarket; users should not need a local path or a terminal command.

dsh-session-grove README · dshmarket (recommended)：Updates are owned by dshmarket / the plugin manager. The plugin does not self-update and does not know where its next version is hosted. If you previously installed a local tarball, reinstall once from the market so the installed source is bound to the catalog.

dsh-session-grove README · Upgrading from `dsh-session-groups`：The `0.4.0-beta.1` identity reset means this package does **not** auto-read, copy or delete the old `dsh-session-groups` record or browser keys; this avoids importing data from the same-named community plugins. The manual migration checklist is in [docs/MIGRATION-0.4.md](docs/MIGRATION-0.4.md).

dsh-session-grove README · Maintainer/developer install：Local tarball and command-line installation are maintainer/debug workflows only. They are documented in [docs/RELEASE.md](docs/RELEASE.md); ordinary users should use the market entry.

dsh-session-grove README · Data：Uninstalling the plugin restores the shipped workspace view. The group record and local preferences remain and are restored on reinstall. To remove all traces, delete the record, `.bak`, the control token, the diagnostics/debug NDJSON files (if any) and the localStorage keys above.

dsh-session-grove README · Configuration：The plugin manager exposes five switches, all off by default. They live on the first layer of the **Plugins → dsh-session-grove** detail page; no component-row drill-down is needed. All controls use the standard DSH `Switch` and `Tooltip`.

dsh-session-grove README · Configuration：| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `diagnostics` | off | drag HUD and local NDJSON trace; applies live |
| `debugProbe` | off | temporary dialog layout probe and `.debug.ndjson` route; never enable in production |
| `controlApi` | off | master switch for the native `session_grove_control` tool and browser/debug control routes |
| `controlDestructive` | off | allow destructive control operations such as group deletion; requires explicit confirmation |
| `controlSessions` | off | allow session rename and archive changes; requires `controlApi` |

dsh-session-grove README · Configuration：`debugProbe` routes stay registered but return `404 debug-disabled` when off and never write a debug file.  
`diagnostics` routes stay registered but reject writes when off; enabling/disabling updates the client HUD on the next configuration refresh.  
`controlApi` routes stay registered but return `404 control-disabled` when off; when enabled they are local-only and still use the host connection fence.  
Background job monitoring was rolled back in 0.3.0-beta.1; the plugin does not subscribe to `ctx.jobs`.

dsh-session-grove README · AI control：The primary AI channel is the Host-native tool:

```text
session_grove_control
```

It runs in the DSH Host process, without HTTP, a browser cookie, the control token or the CLI. `controlApi` must be enabled; `controlSessions` controls session rename/archive; `controlDestructive` controls deletion.

dsh-session-grove README · AI control：After every group commit (native tool or HTTP), the Host publishes the new revision through `/dsh-session-grove/events`; browsers reload and reconcile. Returning to the groups view also reloads the latest snapshot.

dsh-session-grove README · AI control：`doctor` is a read-only compatibility diagnostic available even when `controlApi` is off. It returns host capabilities, adapter/version range, control gates, storage paths, storage health (status/revision, backupStatus/backupRevision/backupError, quarantine), service presence and mounted routes.

Tool actions:

```text
catalog
state
resolve
plan

dsh-session-grove README · AI control：`catalog` is a read-only vocabulary reference: icon ids/categories/style,
palette ids/hex/labels, documented `colorHex` input forms and canonical
`#rrggbb`, operation names and limits. It does not read group state.

dsh-session-grove README · AI control：`state` returns a stable `revision`, each group's `id`/`path`/icon/color and sessionIds.  
`resolve` maps a complete path array to an id; missing paths return `group-not-found`, duplicate siblings return `ambiguous-path` with candidates.  
`plan` returns `changes` and `planHash`; `apply` must send the same `planHash` and `baseRevision` and commits with CAS.

dsh-session-grove README · AI control：Appearance input is strict: `icon`/`color` must come from `catalog`, `colorHex` accepts `#RGB`, `RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `RRGGBB` and persists canonical lowercase `#rrggbb`, and `color`/`colorHex` are mutually exclusive. Invalid values fail with `invalid-icon` or `invalid-color` instead of silently falling back.

dsh-session-grove README · AI control：Session actions require an explicit `sessionId`; a missing id is `invalid-session-id` and the plugin never guesses the "most recent" session. Rename supports `expectedTitle`; archive supports `expectedArchived`; archiving a running session requires explicit `stopActivity: true`.

dsh-session-grove README · Copy-paste AI prompts：Enable **AI control API** first; the rename prompt also needs **session operations**. No CLI, HTTP request, cookie or token is involved — paste the prompt into a DSH session and let the agent call `session_grove_control`.

dsh-session-grove README · Batch-create a project hierarchy：> Use `session_grove_control` to create (or reuse) this hierarchy:
>
> `<Project> project group` — icon `server`, color `blue`
> - `Designing` — icon `book`, color `purple`
> - `In development` — icon `play-circle`, color `blue`
> - `Paused` — icon `clock`, color `orange`
> - `Done` — icon `check-circle`, color `green`
> - `Cancelled` — icon `x-circle`, color `red`
>
> Reuse existing groups and add only missing children. Run `state`/`resolve` first; if a path is missing or ambiguous, ask me. Then `plan`, show me the changes and `planHash`, and `apply` with the same `planHash` and `baseRevision`.

dsh-session-grove README · Rename and assign in one instruction：> Rename the current session to `<new title>` and assign it to `<Project> project group / In development` using `session_grove_control`. Use the current session's explicit `sessionId`; never guess it. Rename first, then plan/apply `session.assign`. If either step fails, stop and report which step failed. This is two sequential operations, not one transaction.

dsh-session-grove README · HTTP routes (browser/debug)：These routes are for browser settings pages and local debugging, not the primary AI path:

```text
GET  /dsh-session-grove/control/doctor
GET  /dsh-session-grove/control/catalog
GET  /dsh-session-grove/control/state
POST /dsh-session-grove/control/resolve

dsh-session-grove README · HTTP routes (browser/debug)：The real DSH Desktop host browser fence runs before plugin routes. The CLI exchanges the DSH web cookie using `DSH_WEB_URL` (including `?token=`) and then sends the plugin Bearer token. `doctor` works while `controlApi` is off; other control routes remain behind their own gates:

```powershell
$env:DSH_HOME = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh"
$env:DSH_WEB_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:43120/?token=token-printed-at-startup"
node scripts/session-grove-control.mjs doctor
```

dsh-session-grove README · HTTP routes (browser/debug)：The native tool remains the primary AI path; the CLI is only for local read-only diagnosis and debugging. `doctor` exits non-zero when host compatibility is unsupported, so it can gate pre/post-upgrade scripts.

`group.create` plan results do not contain a `groupId`: ids are generated only during apply; call `state` afterwards to read them.

The plugin writes a local control token at:

```text
<dshHome>/storages/dsh-session-grove.control-token
```

dsh-session-grove README · HTTP routes (browser/debug)：The POSIX mode is `0600`. Windows does not enforce POSIX modes as ACLs; on a multi-user machine verify the effective ACL separately. When `controlApi` is off, control routes other than `doctor` still return 404; the token cannot bypass the host browser fence.

dsh-session-grove README · HTTP routes (browser/debug)：The bundled skill is `skills/session-grove-control/SKILL.md`. When `controlApi` is enabled, the plugin installs it to `<dshHome>/skills/session-grove-control/SKILL.md`; the settings card can verify or repair a missing/damaged managed skill without reinstalling the plugin. A user-owned file with the same name is never overwritten.

Diagnostics are written to:

```text
<dshHome>/storages/dsh-session-grove.diagnostics.ndjson
```

dsh-session-grove README · HTTP routes (browser/debug)：Only while `diagnostics` is on. It contains drag events, ids and timings, never session transcripts. The file is truncated to empty before an append would grow it past 8 MiB; it is not rotated.
